title: 다 듣고 보니 알겠어요: -고서·-고 보다·-고 들다·-고 해서
objective: By the end, you can tell the meanings of -고서, -고 보다, -고 들다 and -고 해서 apart, and you can use each one correctly in a sentence.
summary: This worksheet compares four connecting patterns: -고서 (after doing), -고 보다 (realizing after doing), -고 들다 (pushing hard or persistently) and -고 해서 (one reason among several).

task.title: Choose, complete and fix
task.line: Read each sentence and choose the right form, write the right form of the word in brackets, or correct the mistake.

forms.when: Use after a verb stem to say: do A first, then B. Both parts have the same subject. A is never in the past tense.
forms.means: after doing A, (then) B. A stronger version of -고 that stresses the order
forms.example: 회의 자료를 다 읽고서 회의에 들어갔어요.
forms.exampleMeaning: I went into the meeting after reading all the meeting papers.

forms.when: -고서야: B happened only after A. -고서는: if A is done (often in a bad way), B is not possible; with -지 않고서는 it means 'without doing A, B is not possible'. B is usually negative.
forms.means: only after A (-고서야) / having done A, B cannot happen (-고서는); without A, B cannot happen (-지 않고서는)
forms.example: 의사 선생님 설명을 듣고서야 마음이 놓였어요.
forms.exampleMeaning: I only felt relieved after I heard the doctor's explanation.

forms.when: Use when you find out something new after doing A. It is often used in the set phrase 알고 보니.
forms.means: now that I have done A, I see / realize B
forms.example: 직접 살고 보니 서울 생활도 괜찮네요.
forms.exampleMeaning: Now that I actually live here, I find life in Seoul is not bad.

forms.when: Use with verbs like 따지다 or 캐묻다 to describe someone who does something hard and keeps on doing it. It usually sounds negative.
forms.means: to go at it hard; to keep pushing (arguing, asking, etc.)
forms.example: 제 동생은 제가 무슨 말만 하면 따지고 들어요.
forms.exampleMeaning: Whenever I say anything at all, my younger brother starts arguing with me.

forms.when: Use to give one reason when there are other reasons too. It often comes after a noun with 도.
forms.means: partly because of A (and other things), so B
forms.exampleMeaning: It was late, among other things, so I took a taxi.

watchOut: 먹었고서 (X) → 먹고서 (O): Never put a past ending before -고서. Show the past tense at the end of the sentence: 먹고서 나갔어요.
먹고 봤어요 (X) → 먹어 봤어요 (O): To say 'tried doing', use -아/어 보다. -고 보다 means 'did it, and then realized'.
친구 집에 가고서 숙제했어요 (X) → 친구 집에 가서 숙제했어요 (O): With 가다/오다, when you do B at the place you went to, use -아서.
exercises: Choose the right form: (알고 보니 / 알고 해서) 그 식당 사장님이 제 고향 사람이었어요.
Fill in the blank with -고서야 (듣다): 선생님 설명을 끝까지 ____ 이해했어요.
Fill in the blank with -고 해서 (없다): 요즘 돈도 ____ 외식을 거의 안 해요.
Fill in the blank with -고 들다 in the present tense (캐묻다): 제 친구는 제가 남자 친구 이야기만 하면 꼬치꼬치 ____.
Find and fix the mistake (keep -고서): 어제 저녁을 먹었고서 공원에서 산책했어요.
Choose the right form: 새로 생긴 빵집 빵을 (먹어 봤는데 / 먹고 봤는데) 정말 맛있었어요.
